standard.title: Integrate reading knowledge
standard.description: read different types of texts, integrating phonic, semantic and grammatical knowledge to read accurately and fluently, re-reading and self-correcting when needed
standard.prior_knowledge: Students read a range of texts accurately and fluently using phonic, semantic and grammatical knowledge (AC9E3LY04). They have not yet practised integrating all three knowledge sources across different text types with self-correction strategies.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can read different text types accurately and fluently by integrating phonic, semantic and grammatical knowledge simultaneously, and apply self-correction strategies — re-reading, pausing, cross-checking — when meaning breaks down.

nodes.label: Three knowledge sources working together
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how phonic, semantic and grammatical knowledge each contribute to fluent reading and how they use all three simultaneously.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain what each of the three knowledge sources does for a reader: phonic (sounds/letters), semantic (meaning), grammatical (sentence structure).
nodes.typical_width: Demonstrate understanding that fluent reading requires simultaneous integration of all three sources, explaining how a reader uses all three when encountering an unknown word — checking sound, meaning and grammatical fit.
wider: Analyse what goes wrong when only one knowledge source is applied (e.g. a phonically correct but semantically wrong word choice) and explain how integration corrects this
Reflect on own reading using the three knowledge sources as a framework, identifying which source is strongest and which needs more attention
nodes.hinge_reason: N2's self-correction strategies require students to know which knowledge source has failed — without the three-source framework, students cannot diagnose breakdowns and apply targeted correction.

response_modes.reason: The concept of three integrated knowledge sources is abstract for Year 4 students who read fluently. Making the integration visible requires explicit reasoning about what each source does and how they cross-check.

success_criteria: Can name and briefly describe all three knowledge sources
Can explain that fluent reading uses all three simultaneously, not one at a time

nodes.label: Self-correction strategies
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and apply self-correction strategies — re-reading, pausing, cross-checking — when reading breaks down.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one self-correction strategy and demonstrate its use when reading a challenging text aloud.
nodes.typical_width: Apply a range of self-correction strategies — re-reading from the start of the sentence, pausing to check meaning, cross-checking across all three knowledge sources — automatically when meaning breaks down in a range of text types.
wider: Reflect on which self-correction strategies are most useful for which types of breakdown (unfamiliar word, complex sentence, unfamiliar topic) and explain why
Apply self-correction strategies to increasingly complex texts, including subject-specific texts from other curriculum areas

response_modes.reason: Self-correction is a fluency habit built through practice. Students who understand the strategies intellectually still need repeated reading practice across texts to internalise them as automatic responses.

success_criteria: Can name at least two self-correction strategies
Demonstrates re-reading or cross-checking when meaning breaks down in reading aloud
